name: White-tailed Deer
description: A familiar woodland browser with a bright white underside to its tail. Adults change from warmer summer coats to grayer winter coats.

size.note: Female adult weight: approximately 45–91 kg (100–200 lb), from the NPS reference. Males can be larger; this is not a combined-sex range.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: American Black Bear
description: Rounded ears, a short tail, and a brown muzzle distinguish this powerful forest mammal. Virginia bears are usually black-coated.

size.note: Adult nose-to-tail length: about 122–213 cm. Combined female/male weight span: about 41–227 kg; season and sex strongly affect mass.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Red Fox
description: A pointed muzzle, upright ears, dark lower legs, and a generous brush of a tail give this adaptable canid its distinctive outline.

size.note: DWR reports approximately 46–89 cm length and 3–14 kg weight; individuals and regional populations vary.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: North American River Otter
description: A streamlined swimmer with short legs, webbed feet, and a strong tapering tail. Its dense brown coat is paler underneath.

size.note: Total length: 90–127 cm; weight: about 4.5–11.3 kg, from DWR. Activity can occur at any hour.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Northern Cardinal
description: A crested songbird with a stout seed-cracking bill. The sprite represents the bright red male; females are warm brown with reddish accents.

size.note: The linked NPS guide describes a small songbird. A numeric length or mass range is not supplied here.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Bald Eagle
description: Adults combine a white head and tail with broad brown wings. Young eagles lack the full adult white-headed pattern.

size.note: NPS gives an average adult length range of about 71–97 cm (28–38 in) and an approximately 203 cm (80 in) wingspan.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Great Blue Heron
description: A long-legged wader with a folded neck in flight and a dagger-like bill. Look for its patient, deliberate stance beside shallow water.

size.note: NPS reports weight around 2.1–2.9 kg and length up to about 137 cm. Wingspan is approximately 168–198 cm.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Pileated Woodpecker
description: A large black woodpecker with bold white face markings and a red crest. It excavates wood in search of insects.

size.note: Body length: 40–49 cm. The NPS bird guide reports weight around 227–340 g (8–12 oz).

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Woodland Box Turtle
description: A high-domed land turtle patterned with yellow or orange. Its hinged lower shell can close around its head and limbs.

size.note: DWR reports 11–20 cm (4.5–8 in). This measurement describes shell length, rather than head-to-tail length.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Central Ratsnake
description: A long, often dark-bodied snake associated with wooded edges. Older references may call this animal an eastern or black ratsnake.

size.note: Names and species boundaries differ among older references. No numeric range is included from those mixed-taxonomy accounts.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Five-lined Skink
description: A sleek, striped lizard that can move quickly into cover. The blue tail shown in the sprite is especially characteristic of young skinks.

size.note: NPS describes adults reaching around 20 cm (8 in); a typical range and mass are not included here.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Eastern Painted Turtle
description: A low, smooth-shelled freshwater turtle with red accents around the shell margin. Basking sites are an important part of its habitat.

size.note: DWR reports shell length up to approximately 18 cm (7.2 in). A maximum is not a typical adult range.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: American Bullfrog
description: A large green-to-brown frog often seen at the edge of permanent water. Its conspicuous round eardrum sits behind the eye.

size.note: NPS reports length up to about 20 cm (8 in) and weight exceeding 0.45 kg (1 lb); these are not typical ranges.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Spotted Salamander
description: A dark, sturdy salamander with rows of yellow spots. Adults spend much of their time sheltered underground.

size.note: The NPS Prince William Forest guide reports approximately 11–19 cm (4.5–7.5 in) total length.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Red-spotted Newt
description: This amphibian changes its look and habitat as it grows. The sprite shows the orange terrestrial eft; aquatic adults are usually olive green.

size.note: DWR reports total length up to about 12 cm (4.8 in). Efts and aquatic adults differ in appearance and habits.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Spring Peeper
description: A tiny frog often marked with a dark X on its back. Its familiar high-pitched calls can be easier to notice than the frog itself.

size.note: DWR reports length up to about 3.2 cm (1.25 in). Not every individual shows a sharply defined X.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Brook Trout
description: A cold-water fish with a patterned back, pale spots, and orange-red fins edged in white. It depends on cool, well-oxygenated streams.

size.note: DWR gives a typical Virginia length of about 15–30 cm (6–12 in). Some individuals grow larger.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Largemouth Bass
description: An olive-green ambush predator with a broad mouth and a dark stripe along its side. It often uses submerged cover.

size.note: DWR reports individuals reaching about 7.3 kg (16 lb) in Virginia; this is a maximum, not typical body mass.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Bluegill
description: A deep-bodied sunfish with a dark ear flap and vertical side bars. Colors shift among olive, blue, yellow, and silver.

size.note: No general adult length or mass range is supplied in the linked DWR profile; local fisheries samples are not used as species-wide ranges.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Channel Catfish
description: A smooth-skinned fish with a deeply forked tail and sensitive barbels around its mouth. Deep pools provide useful shelter.

size.note: NPS gives an average length range of approximately 25–51 cm (10–20 in). Larger fish occur.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Monarch Butterfly
description: An orange-and-black butterfly with pale spots around its wing borders. Adults visit flowers; caterpillars depend on milkweed.

size.note: NPS gives wingspan around 8.4–9.4 cm (3.3–3.7 in). Wingspan is not body length.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Eastern Tiger Swallowtail
description: A broad-winged butterfly often yellow with bold black stripes and trailing hindwing tails. Some females have a dark color form.

size.note: A sourced numeric size or mass range is not included in this starter entry.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Common Green Darner
description: A large dragonfly with a green thorax and a long abdomen. Males often show blue abdominal markings; immature and female colors vary.

size.note: The NPS reference reports wingspan around 9–10 cm. Its 68–78 mm measurement describes the abdomen, so it is not presented as total body length.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.

name: Atlantic Horseshoe Crab
description: A marine arthropod with a rounded shield and a long, straight tail. Its coastal life connects shallow-water habitats and migrating shorebirds.

size.note: NPS reports about 36–38 cm for males and 46–48 cm for females, head to tail. This combined span hides the size difference between sexes.

regionNote: Illustrative habitat association; not verified sightings or a distribution map.
